segments.speaker: ada
segments.text: Okay, quick sync on the retrieval eval. Grace, where are we on the benchmark harness?

segments.speaker: grace
segments.text: The harness runs end to end on the small split. The numbers are noisy because we re-embed every run. I'd like to cache embeddings.

segments.speaker: linus
segments.text: Agreed, that also makes the nightly cheaper. Any objection to pgvector for the cache rather than a flat file?

segments.speaker: ada
segments.text: No objection. Decision: we cache embeddings in pgvector, keyed by model name and content hash.

segments.speaker: grace
segments.text: Action: grace will add the embedding cache table and the migration by Friday.

segments.speaker: linus
segments.text: Linus will wire the nightly eval to read from the cache once the table lands.

segments.speaker: ada
segments.text: One more thing. The reviewers asked for a human baseline. Question for linus: do we have budget for a hundred annotated queries?

segments.speaker: linus
segments.text: I'll check the grant line and get back to you. Let's not decide today.

segments.speaker: ada
segments.text: Fine. Also, decision: the paper deadline stays at October 3, no extension request.

segments.speaker: grace
segments.text: Got it. That's everything from me.
